어서 오세요.forms: casual: 어서 와 · formal: 어서 오십시오
어서 오세요.x: Welcome! How many in your party?
어서 오세요.e: Literally 'come quickly' — the greeting you hear walking into any Korean shop or restaurant.

한테.m: to (a person or animal); from (a person)
한테.x: I gave a present to my younger sibling.
한테.t: 한테 is the conversational version of 에게.

고민하다.forms: 고민해요 · 고민했어요 · 고민할 거예요 · 고민하지 마세요
고민하다.m: to agonize over, to think hard about, to worry
고민하다.x: I thought hard for a long time about which clothes to buy.
고민하다.e: Literally 'to suffer bitter anguish', though Koreans use it lightly, even about lunch.

초록색.x: When spring comes, the mountains turn green.
초록색.t: Pronounced [초록쌕]; traffic lights are often called 초록불 or 파란불.

교수.x: My father is a university professor.
교수.t: Always add -님 when speaking to or about your professor: 교수님.

군인.ex: 제 동생은 지금 군인이라서 집에 자주 못 와요.
군인.x: My younger brother is a soldier now, so he can't come home often.
군인.t: Most Korean men serve in the military; 군대에 가다 means to start mandatory service.

고모.ex: 설날에 고모 댁에 가서 세배를 했어요.
고모.x: On Lunar New Year I went to my aunt's house and gave her a New Year's bow.

체크카드.ex: 신용 카드 대신 체크카드를 쓰니까 돈을 덜 쓰게 돼요.
체크카드.x: Since I use a debit card instead of a credit card, I end up spending less.
체크카드.e: Konglish from English 'check' + 'card'; in English it's a 'debit card'.
체크카드.t: The money comes straight out of your bank account, so you can't spend more than you have, unlike a 신용 카드. Banks usually issue one when you open an account.

보고하다.x: I reported the results of today's meeting to the department head.
보고하다.t: When reporting to a superior, 보고드리다 sounds extra polite.

예술.x: I want to study art in college.

투표.ex: 선거 날에는 꼭 투표를 하러 가세요.
투표.x: Be sure to go vote on election day.

내성적.x: I'm introverted, so giving presentations is hard for me.

도전.ex: 외국에서 일하는 것은 저에게 큰 도전이에요.
도전.x: Working abroad is a big challenge for me.
도전.e: Literally 'provoke a fight'; now any challenge you take on.

결심하다.m: to decide, to make up one's mind, to resolve
결심하다.x: I've resolved to quit smoking starting this year.
결심하다.t: 결심하다 is a personal resolution, usually with -기로: 운동하기로 결심하다.

우편.ex: 신청 서류는 다음 주에 우편으로 보내 드리겠습니다.
우편.x: We'll send you the application documents by mail next week.
우편.e: From old relay-station mail service; think 'mail convenience'.

감소하다.x: Traffic accidents have decreased significantly compared with last year.

일으키다.m: to cause, bring about; to raise, help (someone) up
일으키다.ex: 담배는 여러 가지 병을 일으킬 수 있어요.
일으키다.e: Causative partner of 일어나다 'to get up, happen'.

논리.ex: 그 사람의 말은 논리가 맞지 않아요.
논리.x: What that person says doesn't make logical sense.
논리.t: Pronounced [놀리] — ㄴ before ㄹ becomes ㄹ (liquidization).

원만하다.x: The two of them settled the problem amicably.
원만하다.e: Literally 'round and full' — no sharp edges, nothing missing.
원만하다.t: Often used as 원만하게 해결하다 'settle amicably' or 대인 관계가 원만하다 'gets along with people'.

잔디.x: We sat on the grass and ate our packed lunch.
잔디.e: Native word. 잔디밭 = a lawn, a grassy field (밭 'field').
잔디.t: 풀 is grass or weeds in general; 잔디 is the short, planted kind. Keep-off signs say 잔디에 들어가지 마세요.

살금살금.x: I tiptoed so the baby wouldn't wake up.
살금살금.e: Manner word (의태어) for moving quietly so no one notices. Dark-vowel 슬금슬금 is the standard pair, with a more furtive, sly feel.
살금살금.t: Typically with movement verbs: 살금살금 다가가다 'to creep up on'.

인감.ex: 집을 살 때는 인감 증명서가 필요합니다.
인감.x: When you buy a house, you need a seal certificate.
인감.e: A seal registered with the government so others can check that it's genuine.
인감.t: Koreans traditionally use a registered stamp (인감 도장) instead of a signature for big contracts.

드러내다.m: to reveal, to show, to expose
드러내다.ex: 그는 자기 감정을 잘 드러내지 않아요.
드러내다.x: He doesn't show his feelings much.
드러내다.e: Active partner of 드러나다 'to be revealed'.

내면.x: It's important to look at a person's inner self.
내면.e: Literally 'inside face': the side of a person others can't see.

예선.x: Our school's team made it through the qualifying round.

의결.x: This item was voted on and approved at the plenary session of the National Assembly.

자치.ex: 지방 자치가 다시 시작된 지 30년이 넘었어요.
자치.x: It has been over thirty years since local self-government started again.

타개하다.m: to break through, to overcome (a deadlock or crisis)
타개하다.ex: 회사는 위기를 타개하기 위해 새로운 전략을 세웠습니다.
타개하다.x: The company set up a new strategy to break through the crisis.
타개하다.e: Literally 'striking it open' — smashing through a blocked situation.
타개하다.t: Typical objects: 위기, 난국, 교착 상태 (crisis, impasse, deadlock); 타개책 means a way out.

결렬되다.m: to break down, to collapse (talks, negotiations)
결렬되다.x: The negotiations broke down due to differences between the two sides.
결렬되다.e: Literally 'burst and split' — talks tearing apart.
결렬되다.t: Used almost only with talks: 협상, 회담, 교섭이 결렬되다.

내던지다.m: to throw away, to fling, to toss; to give up (one's life or position)
내던지다.ex: 그는 화가 나서 가방을 바닥에 내던졌어요.
내던지다.x: He got angry and flung his bag on the floor.
내던지다.e: 내- 'out' + 던지다 'to throw': hurling something away.

가히.forms: 가히 + noun + -(이)라 할 만하다 / -(이)라 할 수 있다
가히.m: truly, indeed (it can fairly be said)
가히.ex: 그의 연주는 가히 최고라고 할 만했어요.
가히.x: His performance could truly be called the best.
가히.e: 'Can, worthy' plus the adverb ending -히: 'it can truly be said'.
가히.t: Almost always followed by -라 할 만하다 or -라 할 수 있다.

고분고분.ex: 그 아이는 부모님 말씀을 고분고분 잘 들어요.
고분고분.x: That child listens to his parents obediently.

삼삼오오.forms: 삼삼오오 모이다 · 삼삼오오 짝을 지어 (no particle)
삼삼오오.m: in small groups, in twos and threes
삼삼오오.ex: 점심시간이 되자 직원들이 삼삼오오 식당으로 향했어요.
삼삼오오.x: When lunchtime came, the employees headed to the cafeteria in small groups.
삼삼오오.e: Literally 'threes and threes, fives and fives' — small scattered groups.
삼삼오오.t: Used like an adverb with no particle: 삼삼오오 모여 앉다.

불철주야.m: day and night, around the clock
불철주야.ex: 소방관들은 불철주야 시민의 안전을 위해 일합니다.
불철주야.x: Firefighters work around the clock for the safety of citizens.
불철주야.t: Mostly adverbial in formal praise: 불철주야 노력하다 'to work tirelessly.'

시시비비.m: right and wrong; the rights and wrongs of a matter
시시비비.ex: 두 회사는 법원에서 시시비비를 가리기로 했어요.
시시비비.x: The two companies decided to settle who was right in court.
시시비비.e: Literally 'call right right, call wrong wrong.'
시시비비.t: Set phrase: 시시비비를 가리다 or 따지다 'to determine who's right and who's wrong.'

체면.x: I couldn't say I didn't know because I didn't want to lose face.
체면.e: Literally 'body and face' — how you appear to others.
체면.t: 체면을 차리다 = to keep up appearances; 체면이 서다 / 구기다 = to save / lose face.

상승세.m: upward trend, rising momentum; winning streak
상승세.ex: 집값이 석 달째 상승세를 이어가고 있습니다.
상승세.x: Housing prices have continued their upward trend for three months.
상승세.t: Also used in sports for a team on a roll: 상승세를 타다 (to ride a winning streak).

탈고.m: finishing a manuscript, completing a draft
탈고.x: The author finished the manuscript of the novel after three years.
탈고.e: Literally 'shedding the manuscript' — finally done with it.

수려하다.m: beautiful, handsome, fine (of scenery or looks)
수려하다.ex: 이 지역은 산과 물이 수려하기로 유명해요.
수려하다.x: This area is famous for its beautiful mountains and rivers.

지순하다.ex: 어머니의 지순한 사랑은 무엇과도 바꿀 수 없어요.
지순하다.x: A mother's utterly pure love can't be traded for anything.

보도지침.x: In the 1980s, the government controlled the press with reporting directives.
보도지침.e: Literally 'reporting compass needle'; recalls the secret press orders of the 1980s military regime.

봉사정신.ex: 그 간호사는 투철한 봉사정신으로 환자들을 돌봤어요.
봉사정신.x: That nurse cared for patients with a deep spirit of service.
봉사정신.e: Literally 'serving spirit'; 봉사 alone also means volunteer work.

기구하다.ex: 할머니는 전쟁을 겪으며 기구한 삶을 사셨어요.
기구하다.x: Grandma lived a life full of hardship through the war.
기구하다.e: Literally 'rugged and steep', like a mountain trail.
기구하다.t: Almost always with 운명, 삶 or 인생: 기구한 운명 'a cruel fate'.
